rationale: The workflow already implements the applicable dependency-caching optimization: `ruby/setup-ruby@v1` is called with `bundler-cache: true`, which caches Bundler dependencies (Gemfile.lock-keyed, Ruby-version-scoped) and satisfies the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern's intent of caching dependency downloads while keeping installation and all required tests. The matrix already has `fail-fast: false`, so remaining matrix jobs are not cancelled after a failure, consistent with preserving full test coverage across Ruby versions. No representative CI duration history is available (ci_history is marked `not_a_measured_baseline` with no run durations), so custom or history-based timeouts (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT) cannot be justified. Path-based trigger filtering (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER) is contraindicated because the shared Gemfile.lock and multi-Ruby-version matrix mean changes to any file can affect all test cells. Adding a redundant explicit `actions/cache` step for `vendor/bundle` on top of `bundler-cache: true` is not supported as a meaningful additional optimization for this configuration; the experiment evidence showing benefit from an explicit cache step involved a workflow with an additional gemfile matrix dimension not present here.
